theory.intro: When the **area** of a circle, semicircle, quadrant or sector is known but a length or angle is not, substitute into the formula and work backwards with **inverse operations** until the unknown stands alone.
facts: Circle $A = \pi r^{2}$; semicircle $A = \frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}$; quadrant $A = \frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}$; sector $A = \frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}$.
Undo the operations in reverse order: clear the fraction, then divide by $\pi$, then take the square root last.
$r^{2} = k$ gives $r = \pm\sqrt{k}$, but a radius is a length, so reject the negative solution and state that reason.
To find a **diameter**, find the radius first and then double it.
To find the **angle**, rearrange to $\theta = \frac{360A}{\pi r^{2}}$.
A sector angle lies between $0^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$, so an answer outside that range means no such sector exists.
When the area is given as a multiple of $\pi$, the $\pi$ on each side cancels, often leaving an exact whole-number radius.
steps: Solve for the unknown using inverse operations.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi r^{2}\\80&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{80}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{80}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx5.05\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\32&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\64&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{64}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{64}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx4.514\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\18&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\72&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{72}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{72}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx4.79\text{ mm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi r^{2}\\50&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{50}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\text{ mm}$.
Double the unrounded radius.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\\d&\approx7.98\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\24&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\48&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{48}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\text{ cm}$.
Double the unrounded radius.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\\d&\approx7.82\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\16\pi&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\64\pi&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=64\\r&=\pm8\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=8\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}\\27\pi&=\frac{120}{360}\pi r^{2}\\27\pi&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{3}\\81\pi&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=81\\r&=\pm9\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=9\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\times9\\d&=18\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}\\48\pi&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi(8)^{2}\\17280\pi&=64\pi\theta\\\theta&=\frac{17280\pi}{64\pi}\\\theta&=270^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
This is the reflex interior angle of the sector.

The outer radius is $R=24\div2=12\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi R^{2}-\pi r^{2}\\80\pi&=\pi(12)^{2}-\pi r^{2}\\\pi r^{2}&=144\pi-80\pi\\\pi r^{2}&=64\pi\\r^{2}&=64\\r&=\pm8\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=8\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\times8\\d&=16\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

mastery.question_text:
A sector has an area of $96\pi$ cm$^{2}$ and an angle at the centre of $240^{\circ}$.
Find the exact radius.
mastery.solution_text:
$A = \frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}$
$96\pi = \frac{240}{360}\pi r^{2}$
$144\pi = \pi r^{2}$
$r^{2} = 144$
$r = \pm 12$
A radius is a length, so $r = 12$ cm.

mastery.question_text:
A sector has an area of $75\pi$ cm$^{2}$ and a radius of $10$ cm.
Find the interior angle at the centre.

A shape is made up of two circles with the same centre.
The diameter of the larger circle is $20$ cm and the area of the region between the circles is $64\pi$ cm$^{2}$.
Find the exact diameter of the smaller circle.
mastery.solution_text:
The outer radius is $20\div 2 = 10$ cm.
$A = \pi R^{2} - \pi r^{2}$
$64\pi = \pi(10)^{2} - \pi r^{2}$
$\pi r^{2} = 100\pi - 64\pi$
$r^{2} = 36$
$r = \pm 6$
A radius is a length, so $r = 6$ cm.
$d = 2\times 6 = 12\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A sector has an area of $66\pi$ cm$^{2}$ and an angle at the centre of $165^{\circ}$.
Find the exact diameter.
mastery.solution_text:
$A = \frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}$
$66\pi = \frac{165}{360}\pi r^{2}$
$r^{2} = \frac{66\pi\times 360}{165\pi}$
$= 144$
$r = \pm 12$
A radius is a length, so $r = 12$ cm.
$d = 2\times 12 = 24\text{ cm}$
